purpose: User-invoked prose skill (disable-model-invocation: true, SKILL.md:4) that has the agent review a coding session's record and propose environment improvements (navigation pointers, automated checks, reviewer standards, AGENTS.md trimming, tool economy, no-ops, information access), ordered by severity (SKILL.md:7, 15-25).
mechanism:
1. Step 1 loads the `writing-for-agents` skill (current SKILL.md:11). 2. Step 2 reads the session's primary sources, defaulting to the current session (:13). 3. Step 3 walks seven categories, each with a "Use when" trigger (:17-23). Automated checks says to read the repo's own check command and CI first and to treat a repo with no guardrail as a finding (:18). Coding standards says to classify the violation as mechanical or judgement, build a deterministic check for mechanical ones, and keep CODING_STANDARDS.md for judgement calls (:19). 4. Step 4 presents candidates by severity (:25). The Reference section (:27-44) gives the implementation-vs-review framing and file roles. There are no scripts, schemas or state, so it is pure prose. It proposes only and applies nothing.

IDENTITY CHECK. I read both files in full and compared them line by line. Both are 45 lines. Frontmatter, steps, categories and reference text are identical in what I read, and I found no difference. I have no shell, so I could not run cmp or sha256sum. The digest's byte-identical claim (line 5) therefore rests on its sha256 evidence, not on my read. A trailing-whitespace or newline difference is invisible to my read.
fit_and_overlap:
The four do-not-retry triggers (vet note :203-213) against the 2026-10-07 digest status:

(a) Graduation AND executable procedure (vet :205-207). HALF FIRED, so the trigger does not fire. Graduation is true (a7d038f, 2026-09-24, digest :5). The file is identical to c55ee46, so there is still no script, schema or step-level structure, and the "and" clause fails. The note also says "a further prose commit do not reopen this" (:215).

(b) Raw-session-JSONL fixture beating bare and rent-check (:208-210). NOT FIRED, because it has not been run (digest :5). This remains the recorded evidence gap (vet :154-157).

(c) Harness gains a session-end trigger (:211-212). NOT FIRED. ~/.claude/settings.json has no SessionEnd hook (digest :5). Stop has 2 hooks, and the vet note says the only Stop hook is verify-on-stop.js, a verification gate (vet :238-242). The trigger is also conjunctive: it needs a body of doctrine to hang on the trigger AND rent-check's scope to be demonstrably too narrow. The vet note says adopting retro would not close the trigger gap anyway, because retro is manual (:240-242). The aihero FAQ agrees: no hooks, manual only.

(d) rent-check unavailable or narrowed out of categories 3, 4, 6 (:213). NOT FIRED. rent-check is present (digest :5, :15). Open defect #1244 is a write-boundary defect, not unavailability or a scope narrowing.

Net: no trigger fires. One is half-met, and the missing half is the substantive one. The 2026-09-20 SKIP stands on its own stated terms.

Incumbent coverage per category, from the vet note (:177-184): coding standards, CLAUDE.md size and no-ops are covered by rent-check (RUBRIC E1/E2, Q1/Q2), via the user-invoked /rent-check control surface. Navigation, tool economy and information access have no covering mechanism, but the 2026-09 fixture showed bare, retro and rent-check all found those defects (vet :187-191), so the demonstrated need is nil. Automated checks are partly covered by rent-check E4. The digest says coverage is unverified and defaults to REFUTED. I did not re-verify the vet note's coverage claims today.
